Technical notes (initial):

1) CIDR guidance
- Prefer non-overlapping /16 or /20 at account level, allocate /24 per environment for interface endpoints. Example suggestion if you want a private block: 10.50.0.0/16 for redwood-managed endpoints, then 10.50.1.0/24 (prod), 10.50.2.0/24 (staging)

2) Peering vs TGW
- If Groundline wants cross-VPC access and simplified route management, TGW is recommended (we will present TGW and cross-account attachments).
- For a single VPC integration, VPC peering is lower ops but does not scale as well for multiple VPCs.

3) Private endpoints
- We will provide Interface endpoints that create ENIs in your subnet. Ensure subnet has available IPs for the ENIs (we need at least 3 per AZ for HA).
- Route tables: add routes to the Redwood service CIDR via the ENI. No internet-facing NAT required for control-plane comms once endpoints are present.

4) HSM / KMS
- If the HSM is on-prem, we typically recommend a dedicated interconnect with BGP to the peered VPC or use a transit virtual circuit. We will validate MTU and TLS fingerprints beforehand.

5) Fallbacks & canary plan
- Canary path: deploy a single staging instance behind the private endpoints, validate token auth and throughput. If networking issues occur, we will temporarily route to hosted API via an allowlist for the canary CSR.
- Runbook will include exact rollback commands and expected DNS/route propagation windows.

Attachment: vpc-diagram.png (PNG) — simple sketch of TGW vs peering options.

Action items for Groundline: share account IDs, preferred CIDR block for Redwood endpoints, and confirmation if TGW already exists. Also provide the infra Slack channel for during-cutover coordination.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
